scenarios.title: Zero-touch enterprise onboarding with SSO and data residency
scenarios.tagline: A signed enterprise contract becomes a dedicated, region-pinned, SSO-enabled tenant by the next morning, with no tickets.
scenarios.trigger: A deal closes in the CRM: Enterprise tier, EU data residency, customer IdP (Entra ID) for SSO.

steps.action: Reads the new row in the Signups sheet, then validates the contract fields: tier, region and IdP metadata URL.
steps.checkpoint: The row has a valid tier, region and IdP metadata URL; the bot comments 'Validated'.

steps.action: Runs tenancy-review on the request. Enterprise means the silo model: a dedicated stack pinned to eu-central-1 and a KMS key per tenant.
steps.checkpoint: Review output: model = silo, region = eu-central-1, KMS key per tenant; no blocking findings.

steps.action: Dry run: tenant record, admin user with custom:tenantId, usage plan, Bedrock application inference profile in the EU region.
steps.checkpoint: Dry-run output lists the tenant record, admin user, usage plan key and inference profile, all in eu-central-1.

troubleshoot.symptom: The dry run shows us-east-1 resources
troubleshoot.cause: AWS_REGION was not set from the tenant record
troubleshoot.fix: Export the region from the tenant record before calling tenantctl; add a region check to the skill.

troubleshoot.cause: The base model ARN isn't available in the target region
troubleshoot.fix: Use the region's model or inference-profile ARN; list them with `aws bedrock list-inference-profiles`.

steps.action: Approves the plan in the Slack thread.
steps.checkpoint: Approval recorded in the thread with the approver's name and a timestamp.

steps.action: Deploys the silo stack with CDK in the EU account, then runs onboarding and registers the customer IdP as a Cognito SAML provider.
steps.checkpoint: `cdk deploy` succeeds; `tenantctl.sh status t-…` shows ACTIVE; a SAML provider exists in the tenant's user pool.

troubleshoot.symptom: Users get a SAML error on first login
troubleshoot.cause: IdP metadata URL or attribute mapping is wrong
troubleshoot.fix: Re-import the metadata; map the IdP group claim to `custom:tenantId` only through a trusted pre-token Lambda, never user-editable.

steps.action: Runs the isolation and residency smoke suite: no data outside the EU, and cross-tenant probes return 403/404.
steps.checkpoint: Isolation suite green; the residency check finds no resources or objects outside eu-central-1.

troubleshoot.symptom: Residency check flags a CloudWatch log group in us-east-1
troubleshoot.cause: A global service (or default) wrote logs outside the region
troubleshoot.fix: Pin logging destinations in the silo stack; add an SCP denying other regions for the tenant account.

steps.action: Posts a welcome pack and an audit summary on the row, then sets Status = Live.
steps.checkpoint: Row status = Live with an audit summary comment.

guardrails: Silo deploys need a human approval
Region allow-list per tenant record; SCPs deny other regions in the tenant account
Onboarding is idempotent (conditional writes)
Every step logged with the approver
scenarios.outcome: Enterprise tenants go live in hours, not weeks, and every one is provisioned the same way.
metrics: Onboarding steps done by a human
scenarios.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant CRM as Signups sheet
  participant Bot as Crew intake bot
  participant Arch as architect agent
  participant H as Ops lead
  participant P as Pipeline + tenantctl
  participant QA as qa agent
  CRM->>Bot: Enterprise · EU · Entra SSO
  Bot->>Arch: tenancy-review
  Arch-->>Bot: silo, eu-central-1, KMS per tenant
  Bot->>P: DRY_RUN onboard
  P-->>Bot: planned calls
  Bot->>H: approve?
  H-->>Bot: yes
  Bot->>P: deploy silo stack + onboard + SAML
  P->>QA: isolation + residency suite
  QA-->>Bot: green
  Bot->>CRM: Live + audit summary

paths.name: Approval denied: contract mismatch
paths.when: The ops lead spots that the contract says premium, not enterprise

steps.action: Rejects with a reason in the thread.
steps.checkpoint: Rejection reason recorded; no AWS calls were made after the dry run.

steps.action: Sets the row to 'Needs sales review', tags the account owner and stops.
steps.checkpoint: Row status updated; the bot doesn't retry automatically.

steps.action: Fixes the tier in the CRM, which re-queues the row.
steps.checkpoint: The next bot run starts again at step 1.

paths.outcome: Nothing is provisioned on bad input; the record of why is on the row.

paths.name: Residency test fails after provisioning
paths.when: The qa agent finds tenant data replicated to another region

steps.action: Reports the failing object or resource and blocks the Live status.
steps.checkpoint: Row stays 'Provisioning'; the finding is linked.

steps.action: Finds the cause (e.g. a cross-region backup rule) and proposes an IaC fix.
steps.checkpoint: A PR with the region-pinned config and a test.

steps.action: Redeploys the stack and deletes the out-of-region copy, then re-runs the suite.
steps.checkpoint: Suite green; row moves to Live.

steps.action: Confirms the deletion evidence for the customer's DPA file.
steps.checkpoint: Evidence attached to the tenant record.

paths.outcome: The violation is caught before go-live and documented.

paths.name: Edge case: tenant id already exists
paths.when: The customer already had a basic-tier trial under the same id

steps.action: Conditional put fails, so it logs `onboard.exists` and continues idempotently.
steps.checkpoint: No overwrite of the existing record.

steps.action: Treats it as an upgrade: plans a tier change and silo migration instead of a new tenant.
steps.checkpoint: Plan shows upgrade + data migration steps.

steps.action: Approves the upgrade plan.
steps.checkpoint: Approval recorded.

paths.outcome: The trial becomes the enterprise tenant without duplicate identities.

scenarios.title: 2 a.m. noisy neighbour, mitigated in minutes
scenarios.tagline: One tenant's batch job degrades every premium tenant. Agents find it, propose a scoped throttle, and the on-call engineer approves from their phone.
scenarios.trigger: A CloudWatch anomaly alarm fires: premium-tier p95 latency is above its band.

steps.action: Sees the alarm and starts the sre agent with the tenant-incident skill for the last 60 minutes.
steps.checkpoint: An incident thread exists; the agent posts 'Investigating premium p95, window 01:10–02:10 UTC'.

steps.action: Scopes the problem to the premium tier. The noisy-neighbour query shows t-globex2 at 61% of requests and 9x its usual AI tokens.
steps.checkpoint: Query output shows one tenant with a disproportionate share of Requests/AITokens in the window.

troubleshoot.cause: Service isn't emitting EMF with the TenantId dimension
troubleshoot.fix: Add `emit_usage()` from lab 47; meanwhile filter by the tenant claim in access logs.

troubleshoot.cause: Cause is shared infrastructure, not a tenant
troubleshoot.fix: Take the 'Not a tenant' path: investigate dependencies and deployments instead.

steps.action: Correlates the spike with t-globex2's new nightly export job and shared DynamoDB partition throttling.
steps.checkpoint: Root cause hypothesis names a specific change (new job) and resource (partition), with trace links.

steps.action: Proposes a mitigation: move t-globex2's API key to a stricter usage plan for 4 hours. No global change.
steps.checkpoint: Dry-run shows a single API key moving to the strict plan with an expiry time.

steps.action: Approves on mobile. The throttle is applied, and premium p95 recovers within 6 minutes.
steps.checkpoint: Premium p95 back inside the anomaly band within 10 minutes.

troubleshoot.symptom: p95 doesn't recover after the throttle
troubleshoot.cause: The tenant's traffic wasn't the real cause, or a backlog is still draining
troubleshoot.fix: Check queue depth and DynamoDB throttles; revert the throttle if it didn't help.

steps.action: Drafts a customer-safe note to t-globex2's account manager explaining the throttle and suggesting off-peak scheduling.
steps.checkpoint: Draft message is in the account manager's queue, not sent.

steps.action: Runs runbook-from-incident, which produces a per-tenant write-capacity alarm and a spec task for adaptive throttling.
steps.checkpoint: PR with the new alarm + a spec task exists and links the incident.

guardrails: Investigation is read-only
Mitigation is scoped to one tenant and time-boxed
A human approves every throttle change
The customer message is reviewed before it is sent
scenarios.outcome: One tenant is temporarily limited instead of every tenant degrading, and the class of incident is prevented next time.
scenarios.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant CW as CloudWatch alarm
  participant HB as Crew heartbeat
  participant SRE as sre agent
  participant DA as DevOps Agent (Omni)
  participant H as On-call
  participant T as tenantctl
  CW-->>HB: premium p95 anomaly
  HB->>SRE: tenant-incident 60m
  SRE->>SRE: noisy neighbour query → t-globex2
  SRE->>DA: correlate
  DA-->>SRE: nightly export + partition throttling
  SRE->>H: throttle t-globex2 4h?
  H-->>SRE: approve
  SRE->>T: move key to strict plan
  SRE->>SRE: runbook + alarm + spec task

paths.name: Not a tenant: a bad deploy
paths.when: No tenant stands out; all premium tenants are slow equally

steps.action: Checks deployments and config changes in the window via CloudTrail and the pipeline history.
steps.checkpoint: Finds a deploy 12 minutes before the alarm.

steps.action: Correlates the latency with a new N+1 query in that release.
steps.checkpoint: Root cause with trace evidence.

steps.action: Rolls back the release.
steps.checkpoint: p95 recovers; the rollback is recorded.

steps.action: Runbook + regression test task; adds a latency gate to the pipeline.
steps.checkpoint: PR adds a performance check.

paths.outcome: The fix is a rollback, not a throttle. The skill's scope check prevents punishing an innocent tenant.

paths.name: Edge case: the noisy tenant is enterprise
paths.when: The tenant causing the load has an enterprise SLA

steps.action: Proposes isolating the workload instead of throttling (e.g. dedicated queue or capacity), because throttling would breach the SLA.
steps.checkpoint: Two options with SLA impact noted.

steps.action: Chooses temporary dedicated capacity and pages the account manager.
steps.checkpoint: Decision logged.

steps.action: Deploys the dedicated consumer for that tenant.
steps.checkpoint: Other tenants recover; the enterprise tenant keeps its SLA.

paths.outcome: Tier-aware mitigation that respects contracts.

paths.name: Nobody approves within 15 minutes
paths.when: The on-call engineer doesn't respond

steps.action: Escalates to the secondary on-call through the paging tool; does not apply the throttle itself.
steps.checkpoint: Escalation sent; no automatic mutation.

steps.action: Approves the throttle.
steps.checkpoint: Approval recorded; mitigation proceeds from step 5.

paths.outcome: Agents never self-approve mutations; escalation is automatic.

scenarios.title: A cross-tenant RAG leak caught before release
scenarios.tagline: A retrieval refactor drops the tenant filter. The eval gate's isolation probes catch it in CI, and no customer ever sees it.
scenarios.trigger: A PR refactors the search tool to support hybrid search and accidentally drops kb_filter(ctx).

steps.action: Runs the spec gate, unit tests and the isolation suite. The RAG isolation probe for tenant A asking about tenant B's documents returns B's chunks.
steps.checkpoint: The CI job `test` fails on `@isolation rag: tenant A cannot retrieve tenant B` with B's document ids in the output.

troubleshoot.symptom: The isolation test passes even though the filter was removed
troubleshoot.cause: Seed data has only one tenant, or both tenants share documents
troubleshoot.fix: Seed two tenants with distinct documents and assert on tenantId of every retrieved chunk.

troubleshoot.cause: Retrieval is semantic, so B's chunk sometimes ranks low
troubleshoot.fix: Query with B-unique phrases and check all top-k results, not just the first.

steps.action: Its tenancy review flags that the filter is now a parameter the model can control, not a closure, and cites the tenancy-review rule.
steps.checkpoint: PR comment from the architect agent cites the tenancy-review rule and the file and line.

steps.action: isolation_probes_passed < isolation_probes, so the release is blocked.
steps.checkpoint: Gate output: 'failed tenant-isolation probes'; status check red.

steps.action: Restores kb_filter as a closure and adds a deterministic 'no foreign tenant id in output' check to the golden set.
steps.checkpoint: New commit restores the closure filter; the golden set gains a 'no foreign tenant id in output' check.

steps.action: Reviews the fix and the new probe, then approves.
steps.checkpoint: Approval from security; all checks green.

guardrails: Isolation probes are a hard gate
The tenant filter is never a model-controlled argument
Gateway policy requires tool tenant_id = caller claim
scenarios.outcome: The leak never reaches production, and the eval set permanently covers this class of bug.
metrics: Isolation probe coverage per AI feature
scenarios.diagram:
flowchart LR
  PR[PR: hybrid search refactor] --> CI{AI SDLC pipeline}
  CI --> ISO[isolation probe: A asks about B]
  ISO -->|B chunks returned| BLOCK[release_gate: BLOCKED]
  CI --> REV[architect agent: filter now model-controlled]
  BLOCK & REV --> FIX[ai-engineer: restore closure filter + new deterministic check]
  FIX --> SEC{Security review} --> MERGE[merge]

paths.name: What if it had reached production?
paths.when: The isolation probe was missing and the change shipped

steps.action: An online evaluator with a deterministic 'foreign tenant id in output' check fires.
steps.checkpoint: Alert with session ids.

steps.action: Disables the feature flag for all tenants immediately.
steps.checkpoint: Feature off within minutes.

steps.action: Lists affected sessions and tenants from traces (tenant.id, prompt version).
steps.checkpoint: Impact list for legal and support.

steps.action: Runs the breach-notification process for affected tenants.
steps.checkpoint: Notifications per contract and regulation.

steps.action: Adds the missing probe to the golden set and the gate, so it's never missing again.
steps.checkpoint: Gate updated; postmortem filed.

paths.outcome: Why the CI probe matters: the production path is expensive and painful.

paths.name: Backstop: Policy blocks a tool-level leak
paths.when: The leak was through an agent tool call, not retrieval

steps.action: Cedar rule denies a tool call whose tenant_id differs from the caller's claim.
steps.checkpoint: Decision log shows DENY with the mismatched tenant ids.

steps.action: Fixes the tool to take tenant_id from context, not from the model.
steps.checkpoint: Denials drop to zero for legitimate traffic.

paths.outcome: Defense in depth: even if code regresses, the gateway refuses cross-tenant tool calls.

scenarios.title: Model deprecation: migrate every tenant without a quality dip
scenarios.tagline: A Bedrock model reaches end of life. The AI platform evaluates candidates per tier, canaries by tenant and promotes, with no outage and no surprise bill.
scenarios.trigger: An announcement that the model behind the premium route will be retired in 90 days.

steps.action: Lists every route, profile and tenant that uses the model, from model_policy.json and the application inference profiles.
steps.checkpoint: Inventory table: routes × tiers × tenants × monthly tokens on the deprecated model.

steps.action: Runs ai-feature-eval for 3 candidate models on each golden set and writes eval records.
steps.checkpoint: Eval records exist for each candidate × tier, with pass rate, faithfulness, isolation, p95, cost.

steps.action: Prices each candidate at current per-tier volume and flags a margin impact for basic.
steps.checkpoint: Cost delta per tier; basic tier margin impact flagged.

steps.action: Picks the candidate per tier, trading quality against margin.
steps.checkpoint: Spec records the choice per tier and the rationale.

steps.action: The release gate passes. Canary is 10% of tenants per tier, and inference profiles are updated via tenantctl.
steps.checkpoint: release_gate passes; canary percent = 10 in model_policy.json; profiles updated.

troubleshoot.cause: Candidate is slower at your output lengths
troubleshoot.fix: Lower max_tokens per tier, enable streaming, or choose the next candidate.

troubleshoot.cause: Application inference profiles copy a fixed model; they can't be edited in place
troubleshoot.fix: Create a new profile per tenant pointing at the new model and switch the resolver, then delete the old ones.

steps.action: Compares online evaluation scores and latency by prompt and model version. The canary is healthy, so it is promoted to 100%.
steps.checkpoint: Omni comparison: candidate ≥ baseline on online evals; promoted to 100%.

troubleshoot.symptom: Online scores look worse only for one language
troubleshoot.cause: Golden set under-represented that language
troubleshoot.fix: Add cases for it, re-run the gate, and keep that tier's canary at 10% meanwhile.

guardrails: No model change without an eval record
Cost increase over 15% needs a budget owner
Deterministic per-tenant canary; rollback = revert the PR
scenarios.outcome: Migration finishes weeks before end of life, with quality equal or better and a known cost impact per tier.
metrics: Eval pass rate vs baseline per tier
Days before end of life completed
scenarios.diagram:
flowchart LR
  EOL[Model EOL notice] --> INV[inventory routes, profiles, tenants]
  INV --> EV[eval 3 candidates × tiers]
  EV --> PRICE[price per tier]
  PRICE --> PM{PM picks per tier}
  PM --> GATE[release_gate]
  GATE --> CAN[canary 10% per tier]
  CAN --> OMNI[Omni online evals]
  OMNI -->|healthy| PROMOTE[100%]
  OMNI -->|regression| REVERT[revert PR]

paths.name: Canary regresses
paths.when: Online evaluation scores for the canary drop below baseline

steps.action: Alarm on helpfulness for model version = candidate.
steps.checkpoint: Alarm names the tier and route.

steps.action: Opens a revert PR for the canary config.
steps.checkpoint: PR sets canary to 0%.

steps.action: Merges the revert.
steps.checkpoint: All tenants back on the baseline model.

steps.action: Clusters the failing sessions into new golden cases, then tries the next candidate.
steps.checkpoint: New eval record for candidate #2.

paths.outcome: Rollback is a config revert; the failures improve the eval set.

paths.name: No candidate meets the bar for basic tier
paths.when: Every candidate is either worse or too expensive for basic

steps.action: Decides to change the basic-tier feature (shorter answers, summary only) instead of the model.
steps.checkpoint: Spec updated for basic.

steps.action: New prompt version for basic, then evaluates and gates it.
steps.checkpoint: Gate passes at the lower cost.

paths.outcome: Sometimes the right fix is product scope, not a model.

scenarios.title: Runaway agent spend stopped at the budget, not the invoice
scenarios.tagline: A tenant's automation loops on an agent endpoint. The token budget caps it, alarms fire and FinOps turns it into a pricing conversation.
scenarios.trigger: Tenant t-initech's integration retries an agent call in a tight loop over a weekend.

steps.action: Atomic conditional updates reject calls once the monthly tier budget is reached, so requests fail fast with a clear error code.
steps.checkpoint: Calls beyond the cap return `budget_exceeded`; the budget item `used` stops increasing.

troubleshoot.cause: Concurrent requests read-then-write instead of the atomic conditional update
troubleshoot.fix: Use TokenBudget.charge (UpdateItem with ConditionExpression) exactly as in lab 48.

troubleshoot.symptom: Legitimate calls blocked at month start
troubleshoot.cause: Budget key uses the wrong period or time zone
troubleshoot.fix: Key by UTC month (`BUDGET#tenant#YYYY-MM`) and test the rollover.

steps.action: The per-tenant AITokens alarm fires for t-initech.
steps.checkpoint: Alarm `ai-tokens-spike-t-initech` in ALARM state.

steps.action: Confirms the spend in Cost Explorer under the tenantId tag and finds the looping caller in the traces.
steps.checkpoint: Cost Explorer filtered by tag tenantId = t-initech confirms the spike; the looping caller id is in the traces.

troubleshoot.symptom: Cost Explorer shows no tenantId breakdown
troubleshoot.cause: Cost-allocation tag not activated or calls don't use the tenant's profile
troubleshoot.fix: Activate the tag in Billing; route calls through the application inference profile.

steps.action: Writes a margin impact summary and recommends an overage add-on or the enterprise tier.
steps.checkpoint: Report shows margin impact and two commercial options.

steps.action: Contacts the customer with the fix (backoff) and the commercial options.
steps.checkpoint: Customer contact logged with the backoff guidance.

guardrails: Hard budget per tenant and tier
Per-tenant cost attribution via inference profiles
Agents never change budgets or prices
scenarios.outcome: The bill stays bounded, the customer gets a fix, and pricing learns from real usage.
metrics: Time from anomaly to customer contact
scenarios.diagram:
flowchart LR
  LOOP[t-initech retry loop] --> BUD{TokenBudget}
  BUD -->|over cap| FAIL[fail fast: budget_exceeded]
  BUD --> ALM[AITokens alarm]
  ALM --> SENT[Crew cost sentinel]
  SENT --> FIN[finops agent: margin + options]
  FIN --> AM[Account manager → customer]

paths.name: It's abuse, not a bug
paths.when: Traces show prompt-injection attempts and a leaked API key

steps.action: Rotates the tenant's API key via tenantctl suspend/resume, then tells the tenant admin.
steps.checkpoint: Old key disabled; new key issued.

steps.action: Reviews the endpoint for further abuse paths.
steps.checkpoint: Findings report.

steps.action: Adds a per-key rate alarm and a WAF rate rule.
steps.checkpoint: PR with the new controls.

paths.outcome: The budget limits the damage; the response is security, not billing.

paths.name: Enterprise tenant with contracted overage
paths.when: The contract allows paid overage instead of a hard stop

steps.action: Tier config for this tenant uses a soft cap: alert at 100%, hard stop at 150%.
steps.checkpoint: Calls continue past 100% with overage metered.

steps.action: Generates the overage line items for billing.
steps.checkpoint: Invoice draft.

steps.action: Confirms with the customer before invoicing.
steps.checkpoint: Customer acknowledged.

paths.outcome: Budgets follow the contract, not one global rule.

scenarios.title: Critical CVE across 40 services, patched by an agent fleet
scenarios.tagline: A critical library CVE lands on Friday. The autonomous agent opens tested PRs across every repo, and Security Agent verifies them.
scenarios.trigger: A critical CVE is published for a JSON parsing library used in 40 microservices.

steps.action: Runs a code search for affected repos and versions, then opens one issue per repo from the delegate template with label kiro.
steps.checkpoint: A list of affected repos and versions; one `kiro`-labelled issue per repo using the delegate template.

steps.action: Works the issues in parallel sandboxes: bumps the version, fixes breaking changes and runs tests and isolation suites.
steps.checkpoint: A PR per repo with the bump, fixes and passing tests.

troubleshoot.symptom: Agent PR changes far more than the bump
troubleshoot.cause: Issue scope too loose
troubleshoot.fix: Constrain the template: 'only dependency and directly required code changes; no refactors'.

troubleshoot.symptom: Tests fail on the new major version
troubleshoot.cause: Breaking API change in the library
troubleshoot.fix: Let the agent apply the upgrade guide; if > N files, route to a human owner.

steps.action: Runs on each PR: spec-exempt (security), tests, isolation suite and AI review.
steps.checkpoint: Pipeline green per PR (spec-exempt: security reason recorded).

steps.action: PR security review confirms the vulnerable path is gone. An on-demand pen test runs against the dev endpoint.
steps.checkpoint: Security Agent: vulnerable path not reachable; the pen test reports no exploit.

steps.action: Batch-merges green PRs and rolls out progressively by tier.
steps.checkpoint: All PRs merged; rollout complete across tiers; the dependency scanner shows 0 affected.

troubleshoot.symptom: Error rate rises in the first wave
troubleshoot.cause: Behaviour change in the library (e.g. stricter parsing)
troubleshoot.fix: Rollback alarms revert that wave; add a compatibility shim and re-run.

guardrails: Agents open PRs, humans merge
Sandbox network allow-list
Progressive rollout with automatic rollback alarms
scenarios.outcome: Fleet-wide remediation in hours with evidence for every repo.
scenarios.diagram:
flowchart LR
  CVE[Critical CVE] --> FIND[Kiro: find affected repos]
  FIND --> ISS[40 issues · label kiro]
  ISS --> AA[autonomous agent · parallel sandboxes]
  AA --> PRS[40 PRs]
  PRS --> CI[AI SDLC pipeline]
  PRS --> SA[AWS Security Agent review + pen test]
  CI & SA --> RM{Release manager batch merge}
  RM --> ROLL[progressive rollout by tier]

paths.name: No patched version exists yet
paths.when: The library hasn't released a fix

steps.action: Designs a mitigation: input-size limits and WAF rule blocking the exploit pattern.
steps.checkpoint: Mitigation spec.

steps.action: Deploys the WAF rule and limits fleet-wide.
steps.checkpoint: Exploit pattern blocked at the edge.

steps.action: Watches the upstream repo and reopens the fleet issues when a fix ships.
steps.checkpoint: Issues reopened automatically.

paths.outcome: Exposure is reduced right away, and the patch wave starts automatically later.

paths.name: A repo has no tests
paths.when: The agent can't prove the bump is safe

steps.action: Marks the PR draft and states it can't verify behaviour.
steps.checkpoint: Draft PR with the risk noted.

steps.action: Adds a smoke test or approves a manual check.
steps.checkpoint: Verification recorded before merge.

paths.outcome: Agents surface missing safety nets instead of guessing.

scenarios.title: Customer ticket to deployed fix the same day
scenarios.tagline: A premium customer reports empty exports. Support, engineering and release agents hand off through a bugfix spec, and the customer gets a specific answer before end of day.
scenarios.trigger: Ticket: 'Our CSV exports are empty since Tuesday', tenant t-acme01 (premium).

steps.action: Redacts PII, pulls t-acme01's logs and traces for the window, and finds a serialization error after Tuesday's release. Writes a reproducible bug report.
steps.checkpoint: Bug report with redacted ticket, trace ids for t-acme01, the first failing request time and a reproduction on a test tenant.

troubleshoot.symptom: Can't reproduce on the test tenant
troubleshoot.cause: Data-dependent bug (specific characters or sizes)
troubleshoot.fix: Ask for an anonymized sample via support; replay the exact request shape with synthetic data.

steps.action: Creates a bugfix spec where unchanged behaviour = other export formats. Kiro implements it with a regression test.
steps.checkpoint: Bugfix spec with 'unchanged behaviour' = other formats; regression test fails before the fix and passes after.

steps.action: Adds an isolation case: an export as tenant A never contains B's rows.
steps.checkpoint: New isolation test is in the suite and green.

steps.action: Runs the gates, deploys to dev and runs the smoke tests.
steps.checkpoint: Pipeline green; dev smoke passes.

troubleshoot.symptom: Isolation smoke fails on dev after the fix
troubleshoot.cause: The fix changed the export query's tenant predicate
troubleshoot.fix: Block the release; restore the predicate and add a unit test on the query builder.

steps.action: Promotes the hotfix. Release notes are generated per tier.
steps.checkpoint: Hotfix promoted; release notes list the fix under premium.

steps.action: Drafts a specific customer reply with the root cause in plain terms and the fixed version. A human sends it.
steps.checkpoint: Customer reply draft ready for a human to send.

guardrails: PII redaction before engineering sees the ticket
Reproduction uses a test tenant, never customer data
Humans send customer communications
scenarios.outcome: A same-day fix with a regression test, and a customer reply that builds trust.

sequenceDiagram

  participant S as support agent
  participant D as Developer + Kiro
  participant Q as qa agent
  participant P as Pipeline
  participant R as Release mgr
  C->>S: exports empty
  S->>S: redact · tenant logs/traces · repro
  S->>D: bug + evidence
  D->>D: bugfix spec + fix + regression test

  Q->>P: PR
  P-->>R: green on dev

paths.name: Not a bug: customer configuration
paths.when: Logs show the export filters exclude everything

steps.action: Explains the filter setting with a screenshot-ready answer; no engineering hand-off.
steps.checkpoint: Reply draft with steps.

steps.action: Logs a UX issue: warn when filters return zero rows.
steps.checkpoint: Backlog item linked to the ticket.

paths.outcome: The ticket is resolved in minutes, and the confusing UX goes into the backlog.

paths.name: Many tenants affected
paths.when: Logs show the same error for 30% of premium tenants

steps.action: Escalates to an incident instead of a single ticket.
steps.checkpoint: Incident opened with tenant list.

steps.action: A Guardrails intervention metric and an Omni evaluator flag the session for review.

steps.action: Confirms the attack and notifies the tenant admin; the document stays quarantined.

Tier priority defined in advance
Humans approve quotas and spend

scenarios.title: New regulation: AI transparency and logging per tenant
scenarios.tagline: A regulation requires AI interactions to be disclosed and logged with model, version and purpose, retrievable per tenant on request. Agents turn the legal text into specs, controls and evidence.
scenarios.trigger: Legal confirms new AI transparency obligations apply to the product in 6 months.

steps.action: Summarizes the obligations into a control list with citations to the legal text and internal policies.
steps.checkpoint: Control list with citations; open legal questions marked.

steps.action: Turns controls into specs: disclosure UI, interaction logging, per-tenant export, model registry.
steps.checkpoint: Specs with EARS requirements per control.

steps.action: Designs the logging: every AI call already carries requestMetadata (tenantId, tier) and prompt version; add purpose and model id; store in a per-tenant log stream with retention.
steps.checkpoint: design.md maps each control to a technical mechanism.

troubleshoot.cause: Code paths bypass the tenant_ai.converse wrapper
troubleshoot.fix: Add a lint/CI rule banning direct bedrock-runtime calls outside the wrapper.

steps.action: Implement tasks; CI blocks AI calls without the wrapper.
steps.checkpoint: All tasks ticked; the lint rule is in CI.

steps.action: Tests that a tenant export contains only that tenant's AI interaction log with all required fields.
steps.checkpoint: Export test green.

steps.action: Collects evidence weekly for the control set.
steps.checkpoint: Evidence library updated.

steps.action: Signs off readiness before the deadline.
steps.checkpoint: Sign-off recorded.

guardrails: Legal interprets; agents implement and evidence
Every AI call must go through the tenant-aware wrapper
Per-tenant log isolation tested
scenarios.outcome: Compliance becomes a set of tested controls with continuous evidence instead of a one-off project.
metrics: Time to answer a tenant's transparency request
scenarios.diagram:
flowchart LR
  LAW[Regulation] --> QK[Quick: control list + citations]
  QK --> SPEC[pm: specs per control]
  SPEC --> DES[architect: logging design]
  DES --> BUILD[build + CI lint: wrapper only]
  BUILD --> QA[per-tenant export test]
  QA --> EV[Crew evidence collection]
  EV --> SIGN{Compliance sign-off}

paths.name: The legal text is ambiguous
paths.when: Quick marks two obligations as unclear

steps.action: Requests a legal opinion; the specs implement the stricter reading behind a feature flag.
steps.checkpoint: Both readings documented; strict one implemented.

steps.action: Keeps the looser variant as a backlog item in case the opinion allows it.
steps.checkpoint: Backlog item linked to the legal question.

paths.outcome: Ambiguity doesn't block delivery; the safe interpretation ships.

paths.name: A tenant requests their transparency records
paths.when: Enterprise tenant asks for all AI interaction logs for Q3

steps.action: Runs the per-tenant export for the period, verified against the isolation test.
steps.checkpoint: Export with record counts.

steps.action: Reviews and sends via the secure channel.
steps.checkpoint: Delivery receipt.

paths.outcome: Requests are answered in hours from the same mechanism.

scenarios.title: New engineer ships a tenant-safe change on day one
scenarios.tagline: The repo explains itself: steering, persona kit, skills, team memory and specs let a new hire make a safe, reviewed change on day one.
scenarios.trigger: A new backend engineer joins the payments squad on Monday.

steps.action: Assigns a starter issue that has a spec task and the `good-first-task` label.
steps.checkpoint: Issue links a ticked-off spec context.

steps.action: Session start loads steering, AGENTS.md and team memory (KIRO_MEMORY_ACTOR=payments) and summarizes architecture, conventions and recent decisions.
steps.checkpoint: A briefing that cites ADRs and steering files.

troubleshoot.cause: Custom agent doesn't load steering resources
troubleshoot.fix: Add `file://.kiro/steering/**/*.md` to the agent resources (lab 05).

steps.action: Implements the task with Kiro; hooks lint and test on save; the architect agent reviews tenancy concerns.
steps.checkpoint: Local tests green; review has no blockers.

steps.action: Spec gate, isolation tests, AI review.
steps.checkpoint: All checks green.

steps.action: Reviews and merges; gives feedback that's stored in team memory.
steps.checkpoint: Merged; feedback recorded as a team preference.

guardrails: Same hooks and gates as everyone
Agent permissions deny deploys
Human review on every PR
scenarios.outcome: Onboarding time drops, and the newcomer learns the conventions by doing.
scenarios.diagram:
flowchart LR
  ISSUE[good-first-task] --> BRIEF[Kiro session: steering + team memory briefing]

  CI --> REV{buddy review}

paths.name: Isolation test fails on the first PR
paths.when: The change adds a query without the tenant predicate

steps.action: Isolation test fails; the architect agent comments with the rule and the fix.
steps.checkpoint: Failing test name and rule link in the PR.

steps.action: Fixes it with Kiro and learns the rule; Kiro adds a steering example.
steps.checkpoint: Steering file gains the example; checks green.

paths.outcome: The gate teaches the rule safely, before production.

paths.name: Team memory not configured
paths.when: KIRO_MEMORY_ACTOR isn't set on the new laptop

steps.action: The SessionStart hook prints 'memory unavailable' and continues with steering only.
steps.checkpoint: Session still works; warning visible.

steps.action: Runs the team bootstrap script that sets env vars and installs the agents.
steps.checkpoint: Next session shows team memory.

paths.outcome: The setup fails open and is fixed in one step.

scenarios.title: A fine-tuned model for one enterprise tenant
scenarios.tagline: An enterprise tenant wants answers in its own terminology. Kiro in SageMaker AI fine-tunes on the tenant's approved data, evaluates against the shared model, and routes only that tenant to it.
scenarios.trigger: Enterprise tenant t-globex2 signs an add-on for a domain-adapted assistant.

steps.action: Confirms the data agreement: only the tenant's approved corpus, in their region, never mixed with other tenants.
steps.checkpoint: Signed data-use scope on the tenant record.

steps.action: Model customization skills plan the job: dataset evaluation, transformation, SFT on the tenant corpus in the tenant's account.
steps.checkpoint: Plan notebook with technique SFT and the base model.

troubleshoot.cause: Mixed chat formats in the export
troubleshoot.fix: Use the dataset transformation skill to normalize to one format before training.

steps.action: Evaluates tenant-model vs shared model on the tenant's golden set and the isolation probes.
steps.checkpoint: Eval record: quality uplift on tenant cases; probes pass.

steps.action: Deploys the model and creates an inference profile tagged with tenantId; model_policy routes only t-globex2 to it.
steps.checkpoint: Route resolves to the custom model only for t-globex2.

steps.action: Online evals for t-globex2 sessions by model version.
steps.checkpoint: Scores above the shared-model baseline.

steps.action: Reviews results with the customer.
steps.checkpoint: Customer acceptance recorded.

guardrails: Tenant data never leaves its scope
Routing by tenant in reviewed config
Same eval gate as shared models
scenarios.outcome: A premium, tenant-specific capability that keeps isolation intact.
metrics: Cost per tenant for the add-on

scenarios.title: Spec drift: production behaviour no longer matches the spec
scenarios.tagline: Months of hotfixes have made code and specs disagree. Agents detect the drift, propose which side is right, and humans decide, so specs stay the source of truth.
scenarios.trigger: A support question reveals that pagination behaves differently from requirements.md.

steps.action: Weekly job compares EARS criteria with tests and observed behaviour (contract tests against dev) for each spec.
steps.checkpoint: Drift report: criterion, observed behaviour, evidence.

troubleshoot.cause: Criteria are vague
troubleshoot.fix: Rewrite vague criteria as testable EARS during triage; tag the rest 'informational'.

steps.action: For each drift, proposes whether the spec or the code is right, based on tickets and analytics.
steps.checkpoint: Recommendation per drift with links.

steps.action: Decides each one.
steps.checkpoint: Decision recorded per drift.

steps.action: Update the code or the spec; tests encode the decision.
steps.checkpoint: Spec and tests agree; drift closed.

guardrails: Humans decide intent
Every decision becomes a test
Drift report is read-only
scenarios.outcome: Specs stay trustworthy enough for agents and humans to build on.
scenarios.diagram:
flowchart LR
  SPECS[requirements.md] --> BOT[Crew drift bot: criteria vs tests vs behaviour]
  BOT --> REC[pm: spec or code?]
  REC --> PM{PM decides}
  PM --> FIX[update code or spec + test]

paths.name: Both spec and code are wrong
paths.when: Customers rely on neither documented nor implemented behaviour

steps.action: Defines new behaviour and a migration note for customers.
steps.checkpoint: New criterion + changelog entry.

steps.action: Implement behind a flag, with a deprecation window.
steps.checkpoint: Flagged rollout plan.

paths.outcome: Drift becomes a deliberate product change.

scenarios.title: When an agent misbehaves: kill switch and recovery for the agent fleet
scenarios.tagline: A Crew bot starts commenting on every PR in a loop after a skill change. Org controls stop it in minutes, and the fleet is audited and safely resumed.
scenarios.trigger: Developers report dozens of duplicate review comments from the code-review bot in 10 minutes.

steps.action: Pauses the bot in Kiro Crew and revokes its GitHub token.
steps.checkpoint: No new comments within 1 minute.

steps.action: Signed log shows the bot's actions since the last skill change.
steps.checkpoint: Action timeline with the triggering skill version.

troubleshoot.cause: Bot was running outside Crew (ad-hoc headless job)
troubleshoot.fix: Require all agent automation to run in Crew or CI with logging; block ad-hoc tokens.

steps.action: Diffs the skill change, finds a removed 'skip if already commented' rule, and writes a fix plus an eval case.
steps.checkpoint: Fix PR with an eval reproducing the loop.

steps.action: Approves the fix; the bot resumes in shadow mode for a day.
steps.checkpoint: Shadow-mode output is reviewed and clean.

steps.action: Adds a rate limit per bot (actions/hour) and an anomaly alarm on bot activity.
steps.checkpoint: Alarm fires on a synthetic burst test.

guardrails: Every bot can be paused independently
Skills change via PR with evals
Per-bot rate limits and activity alarms
scenarios.outcome: Agents are governed like production services: observable, interruptible, reversible.
metrics: Time to stop a misbehaving agent
scenarios.diagram:
flowchart LR
  SYM[duplicate comments] --> STOP[pause bot + revoke token]
  STOP --> AUD[audit log timeline]
  AUD --> FIX[skill diff → fix + eval]
  FIX --> SH{approve → shadow mode}
  SH --> LIM[rate limits + activity alarm]

paths.name: The agent took a destructive action
paths.when: The bot closed issues instead of commenting

steps.action: Restores the issues from the audit log list.
steps.checkpoint: All affected issues reopened.

steps.action: Reviews why the token allowed closing; reduces the scope to comment-only.
steps.checkpoint: Token scope reduced.

steps.action: Adds a PreToolUse hook denying close/merge operations for bots.
steps.checkpoint: Hook blocks a test close attempt.

paths.outcome: Least-privilege tokens and hooks prevent a repeat.
